Auf dieses Nachbartreffen kann man getrost verzichten, denn: Anstrengend, aber im negativen wie nervigen Sinne. Kein Vorwurf an den Cast: Alle Vier merkt man die Spielfreude sichtlich an und ist neben der flotten Inszenierung stellenweise auch ansteckend, nur bleiben ihre Figuren zu uninteressant bzw im Falle von Joe und Angela (Wilde, Rogen) fragt man sich, warum die Ehe bisher so lange gehalten hat und andersrum, die biblische Geduld von Piña und Hawk (Cruz, Norton), denn jede:r hätte nach spätestens 15 Minuten bei der (passiv-)aggressiven Stimmung das Weite gesucht. Aber Olivia Wilde setzt weniger auf Glaubwürdigkeit, sondern mehr auf Übertriebenheit und das von Beginn an: Kaum ein Dialog oder Gestik kommt in dem mit unzähligen Sticheleien versehenen Schlagabtausch ohne Hysterie und Theatralik aus. Subilität hat Sendepause und mit Authenzität hat das auch nicht mehr viel zu tun. Sinnbildlich der Score, der die Gefühlslagen stets (über-)präsent sowie penetrant mit schiefen oder sanften Klangteppichen ausrollt. Später, wenn Wilde den Fokus hinter der (bröckelnden) Fassade blicken möchte, bleibt dieser auch verschüchtert. Wer A sagt, muss auch B sagen: Wilde bleibt bei A brav hängen. Allein nur explizit über sexuelle Vorlieben sprechen, ist halt lange nicht mutig genug, provokant erst recht nicht. Entsprechend gestaltet sich Eskalation ernüchternd inkonsequent, noch weniger entlarvend. Stattdessen werden dabei doch wieder die platten Gags rausgeholt. Das ist nicht pointiert, sondern peinlich. Die Komplexität der Konflikte um verschiedene Beziehungsformen und Liebe, aber auch Kommunikationsunfähigkeit, entfaltet sich dadurch selten schlagkräftig, auch da der Film lediglich auf konstruierte Zuspitzung aus ist. Am Ende stehen dann doch wieder Luxusprobleme im Vordergrund und die Tatsache, dass bei aller Offenheit andere Partnerschaftsmodelle außerhalb der traditionellen Ehe, doch nur pervertiert sind und Unruhe reinbringen. Ahja... Aber dann, die letzten 5 Minuten: Die sind plötzlich zutiefst menschlich. Olivia Wilde findet in der Ruhe nochmal leise Töne, die stark beeindrucken! Gerade hier ist zu spüren, was für ein reizvolles Potenzial 'The Invite' besitzt. Hätte sich der Film in den vorherigen 100 Minuten doch mal mehr aus der zahmen (Hollywood-)Komfortzone getraut.

A couple moved a few rows away from us because we were snogging on the back sofa of the cinema as the movie started, and maybe that’s ironic in light of what was to come. Most importantly, The Invite was impossibly bad and lazy in its conception. Absolute failure to construct full-blooded realistic characters, not foolish essentialist tropes of “woman” Vs “man”, or two archetypes for each: woman as neurotic, interior obsessed housewife, woman as totally free uncomplicated sex object/icon; man as useless emotionally repressed stoner, man as sexually liberated metrosexual good guy. As such, there was no opportunity for any character to change grow develop because they were not real enough in the first place. The premise was weak: I didn’t believe in the felt reasoning behind the couples coming together or anything developing between them — as if Penelope Cruz’s character would be interested in that couple. Out of laziness and cowardice they refuse to engage with the wider world, sexual dynamics, gender, class, the New York City teeming beyond their lovely walls. A single location film only works if you can imagine the external world pressing upon it at all times, threatening the controlled conditions. How much better this film would be if just once something from outside burst in — even just the primary couple’s daughter, and so exposing or altering the dynamics at work. Obviously no one who made this film had any clue about polyamory (or desire to ask anyone who did). But I hardly care that the film’s logic argues moving closer to transgressive desire (without fulfilling it) is a way to reinforce and rescue monogamy. I hardly care because there was so much else wrong with the film it feels dull to make the argument that its sexual politics were heteronormative to a fault.

This film kind of plays in the same universe as recent productions like Babygirl or Splitsville . It’s movies that touch up on supposedly steamy and progressive topics but in the end it’s really rather tame and unnecessarily sensationalized for everyone who is not a person with a broad horizon. The setup here is fun. The movie starts at a high level and sticks with it until the third act when it finally crumbles. The editing is quite strong and the performances aren’t bad. At some point I leaned over to my (also homosexual) friend and said: “This is like a regular Tuesday for a queer person,” to which he laughingly agreed. Of course it’s not a regular Tuesday for a queer person (orgies happen more likely on the weekend, just kidding), but it was almost dumbfounding how conservative this film is and yet at the same time thinking it’s pushing boundaries - which it maybe is and I’m just not the target audience. What also really annoyed me were jokes that left a homophobic taste in my mouth. And yeah, the third act really fell apart and it didn’t live up to a potential that was there at some point.

I wouldn’t be surprised if The Invite finds its way into multiple Oscar conversations. I already complimented my favorite aspects in my first review, but man, everything was so well done here. Today’s audience really liked the humor and I think Seth Rogen in particular balanced everything so well, including the humor and facial expressions. Being able to pull off a combination of one of the funniest and most tense movies of the year is special. The way they filmed it — the artsy opening sequence (which also perfectly comes full circle with the ending), the camera/lens choices, the color grading, and the way they framed the characters and utilized foreground and background blur — was so good. The color coordination too. I love how the opening scene goes from them being happy at an undisclosed time to the beautiful frames of Joe just being miserable. This film is an excellent psychological study on self and marriage — communication, opening up, your perspective on the things you have, and resentment. Joe had so many good things going for him, between his daughter, kids learning from him, his musical talent, a pretty wife, and a nice home in San Francisco. He chose to be hung up on the past and push people away. Angela just had communication issues and made Joe feel unheard. You also see that the seemingly perfect couple indeed had their own issues, but Hawk was able to apologize when he was wrong and it was easier for him to be vulnerable. It also just shows how someone like him — someone you could easily judge or put into a box because of his sex life — had his own life experiences that you could empathize with. The end is beautiful because music can really break down barriers and be a language of its own.

no sé ni por donde empezar. dramática, graciosa, humana y con un final… esta opinión no tiene spoilers. la película podría haberse decidido por quedarse solo en la comedia, que lo estaba haciendo a la perfección, pero decide dar un pasó más y agregarle un peso psicológico simplemente deslumbrante. la construcción de toda la historia, para mí, es perfecta. comenzando desde el uso de unos planos súper inteligentes que demuestran desde el primer minuto esa separación “invisible” entre sus protagonistas, algo similar a lo que sucede en parasite (2019) para diferenciar las clases sociales. sumándole a eso una tensión que es genuinamente palpable desde el momento en el que Joe pisa la casa por primera vez, y por último la introducción de cada personaje en escena. la escritura de cada personaje (valga la redundancia) es, en mi opinión, donde radica toda la magia de la película. todos tienen una profundidad terrible, algunos lo demuestran explícitamente en sus diálogos, otros con miradas y algunos simplemente bailando o tocando un piano. pero el hecho de conectar con todos ellos me voló la cabeza, entendes al personaje de Joe y porque reacciona como lo hace, lo mismo su esposa y sus maravillosos vecinos. y esto no lo hacen de una manera brusca, lo hacen entre chistes, entre simples comentarios, y de apoco, sin darte cuenta, conoces de pie a cabeza a todos los que están en esa habitación. es fascinante como pasa de ser una comedia negra, incluso incómoda en varias ocasiones, a un drama psicológico que te lleva a las lagrimas. ¿como un personaje que te hizo reír tanto podría estar tan roto por dentro? ¿como una casa tan perfecta oculta tanto enojo, tristeza y vacío? y destaco particularmente ese detalle de “casa perfecta” porque todo el tiempo se encargan de alagarla, demostrar el esfuerzo que ponen en los detalles, pero todo indica un nivel de superficialidad terrible, demostrado explícitamente en el momento que nos damos cuenta que solo está bien lo que se ve a simple vista, salvo su habitación, su lugar mas personal… al igual que con el drama (2026) que destaque su gran trabajo para representar el sobrepensar, acá debo destacar el increíble trabajo que hacen con la ansiedad y las inseguridades que cargamos con nosotros mismos. la importancia que tiene el amarnos, el sentirnos cómodos en el cuerpo que cargamos y no solo en nuestro físico, sino abrazar nuestros errores, nuestros sueños frustrados, e incluso nuestra infelicidad en muchas ocasiones. y esto no solo por nuestro bien, no solo para que no vivamos miserablemente, sino que estamos tan cegados por nuestro propio odio, que no vemos como estamos lastimando a la persona que mas amamos. si esto lo vivis o lo viviste en primera persona (como yo) pega todo el doble de fuerte, especialmente la angustia que carga el personaje de Joe y Angela. y esta pregunta… ¿como vamos a pedir que nos amen, que nos deseen, si ni nosotros mismos podemos vernos al espejo? todo esto tratado desde el humor, desde la sátira, todo construido lentamente para un final que te parte al medio. ESE momento, un cierre perfecto. lo que destacaría por sobre todas estas cosas es como logran trabajar las inseguridades de AMBOS de igual manera, no odias a uno y amas a otro, entendes a los dos. y eso, aparte de por la gran escritura que tienen y la dirección SUBLIME de Olivia Wilde, es por el enorme peso interpretativo que hay en sus actores, de verdad, lo que hace Seth Rogen y Ella es digno de todas las premiaciones. Penélope Cruz y Edward Norton están espectaculares también. especialmente Norton nos regala la escena en la que vemos el primer quiebre de la película, el momento exacto donde pasa de ser una comedia a un drama TOTAL. y que el personaje de Penélope sea psiquiatra y sexóloga, le da un peso enorme a cada diálogo, e indirectamente nos hacen prestarle más atención a absolutamente todo lo que nos cuenta. un uso espectacular de ambas profesiones. cómo logran ocultar diálogos tristísimos entre carcajadas es digno de pararse y aplaudir. la importancia que pueden tener unos simples tragos, un tequila, un vino, un flan, de cada detalle sacas una lectura, no hay absolutamente nada puesto al azar. busca incomodar, pero te agarra desprevenido. te hace reir, pero al mismo tiempo te hace llorar, te distrae, pero al mismo tiempo te hace mirar para adentro y llevarnos a corregir muchos errores que llevamos con nosotros día a día… y como estos mismos no solo nos arruinan a nosotros, sino que también a las personas que más amamos. me pareció de verdad una película enorme, me encanta como están tratando temas tan psicológicos en el cine actual, como están buscando esa conexión con el espectador y, personalmente, la están logrando al 100%. me dejó sin aliento, pensaba reírme toda la película y termine destruido. todavía me da vergüenza escribir lo que pienso, perdón si me dejo llevar demasiado, es todo realmente pura sinceridad, si otros no conectaron o simplemente no les gustó, esta perfecto también. yo la viví así.

I don’t know what the lesson was meant to be. Strongest aspect of the movie was the comedy. Rogen hilarious, Cruz and Norton are brilliant. Wilde was outclassed from acting perspective (which isn’t saying much paired with 3 heavyweights) but I’m excited about her future as director. There seemed to be an odd general vibe of being a “commentary” but I don’t think it takes a complicated stance. Rogen and Wilde’s characters are miserable - but rogen’s character is evidently a more miserable and toxic partner. There might’ve been a “nobody’s perfect” insinuation but it was clear that Seth rogen’s character was far more imperfect than his wife’s. Usually with these type of relationship-character-driven single set dialogue movies you’ll see the narrative ask the viewer to fall on one side of a fence - but I don’t see what the fence was supposed to be here. This was a couple that probably should divorce. I didn’t see the complicated aspect since there was never a redeeming interaction between them in the brief 2 hours we shared with them. The sexually adventurous, risqué couple (that was more of a metaphor than anything, for what Rogen and Wilde wanted to be - “the grass is always greener”) didn’t shine a new light on the main characters to me. If anything they just told us more of what we already knew. I saw this with Zac and felt that I had to defend my disappointment because he quite liked it. And at its surface, it’s entertaining through its laughs and our wide eyed reactions to the sexual taboos. But on a deeper level I think Olivia Wilde wanted to reflect a sort of societal/romantic commentary. Perhaps on monogamy? On complacency? None of the commentary had an impact on me because it was rooted in a couple that no happy person would ever hope to relate to. At times I thought the movie would be an oddball, weird, shock factor sex comedy. It probably would have landed a better score if not for the “therapy” final act which had me constantly wondering why the second couple had not left an hour prior. I saw don’t worry darling twice and loved it but this one from Wilde tried to (maybe?)  encourage relationship perseverance but gave us no reason to root for them.

Very amusing, beautiful and touching, it spoke to me in a surprisingly introspective way - and stayed with me for a while. It’s a funny, stage play-like movie, focused on its quatuor - not trying to throw too much else at you. It’s contained is what it is. But it’s definitely more than just filmed theatre though. The framing uses mirrors, windows, character positions to express relationships. The colours are meaningful and the photography allows for contrasting warm glows and colder settings. The film’s grain also adds to this timeless and familiar look, totally adapted for a domestic context. And the film spoke to me, made me reflect on my relationship, which was the cherry on the cake. I’ll say the jokes felt sometimes too exaggerated for the grounded characters - like the wine scene. Certain twists were predictable. Also you won’t convince me that Olivia Wilde can be someone who’s uncomfortable about her appearance, but maybe that’s just me. The soufflé bit killed me.

Yes yes yes! Absolutely loved watching this in the cinema! The writing is sharp, the story is simple and the performances are all brilliant, especially from Ed Norton and Penelope Cruz. This gave me a similar feeling as when I watched The Drama as they're both fun drama comedies that make the audience incredibly uncomfortable and actual have something to say. I love how the two couples sit on opposite ends of the emotional spectrum, with one couple perhaps too open and one couple who don't talk enough, so that the audience can debate whether they land on each topic. This is the sort of writing I want to see where the audience aren't spoon fed everything but rather posed questions and ideas and left to make their own decisions on what they agree or disagree with. The soundtrack was strong in parts, particularly the moments of tension, but I felt the more tender moments felt forced with the clichéd sad piano ambience. This reminds of a Hitchcock thriller with its one location, limited cast and storing writing. Id like to think he would have loved this!
